headline: Food chains show energy flow—from sun to plant to herbivore to predator
universal_truth: Everything is connected through what it consumes; you are what you eat, literally
fun_facts: Only about 10% of energy transfers from one level to the next—most is lost as heat
Top predators are rare because so much energy is lost by the time it reaches them
The DDT pesticide accumulated up food chains, nearly killing off bald eagles at the top
discussion_questions: Where are you in the food chain of your industry or field?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: The sun feeds the grass. The grass feeds the rabbit. The rabbit feeds the fox. Energy flows from source to consumer to consumer—this is a food chain. Every creature is connected to every other through what eats what.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Food chains seem simple, but they reveal deep truths about energy, connection, and position. What do they teach us?

options.text: Food chains show that everything depends on what's below it—energy and matter flow through connections; position determines what you can access
options.response: Yes. Where you are in the chain determines your energy sources and vulnerabilities. Understanding chains reveals dependencies and strategic positions.

options.text: They just show what animals eat
options.response: Eating patterns, yes, but also energy flow, dependencies, and system vulnerabilities...

q1.title: Energy Loss
q1.script: Only 10% of energy transfers up each level—90% is lost as heat. That's why there are many plants, fewer herbivores, and even fewer predators. Scarcity at the top is built into physics.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Energy Loss"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Chain Dependencies
q2.script: Remove a link and the chain breaks. If plants die, herbivores starve, then predators starve. Dependencies cascade. What you depend on matters; protect your supply chain.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Your Position
q3.script: You're in food chains too—information chains, value chains, supply chains. Where you sit determines what you access and what depends on you. Position is strategic.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Everything is connected through what it consumes. You are what you eat—literally. Understand your chains and dependencies.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 255. Tomorrow, we'll explore nature's connected eating—food webs. Until then, map your position in one of your chains.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Chain Mapping - Where Are You?
growTrack.activity: Pick a 'chain' you're part of—information, value, supply, influence. What feeds into you? What do you feed into? Where are you positioned? Understanding your chain reveals dependencies and opportunities.
